prerequisites: General knowledge of technical activities within the field of data science and engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge to organize, plan, and manage a project, based on their existing technical knowledge.
Enable students to prepare project-related documents, analyze project feasibility, and handle administrative processing, including the contracting phase.
Know the most used standards for project management and be able to apply them in the context of data science and engineering.
Identify project-associated risks and develop plans for their management.
Enable students to work in multidisciplinary environments and lead work teams in projects.
Enable students to plan and direct innovation projects.
Knowledge of project types, methodologies, and standards.
Be able to document, plan, and budget projects.
Manage human resources of a project.
Contract and bid for projects in compliance with regulations.
Know and apply key aspects in project costs, deadlines, and quality.

syllabus_topics: The project: concept, types, and characteristics.
Methodologies and standards for project management in predictive and adaptive environments.
Preliminary studies and project feasibility analysis.
Project budgeting and cost and risk management.
Group practical work: a project from conception to contracting documentation and other associated documentation.
Individual practical work with planning tools (Microsoft Project).

assessment_methods.method: Group work (memory, reports, oral presentation and defense)
Continuous evaluation: Attendance and participation in seminars and tutorials
Continuous evaluation: Active participation in forums and virtual campus activities
Final in-person knowledge test (test/short questions, application cases, problem solving)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 must be obtained in both the final in-person test and the practical part of the course. Non-completed or non-submitted evaluation activities will count as zero. If the minimum score is not reached in any of the tests, the final numerical grade will be the minimum score of the tests. For the extraordinary call, approved work from the ordinary call will be taken into account; unapproved work will be replaced by an equivalent individual assignment. The final grade will be calculated as 0.65 x In-person test + 0.35 x Work Grade, requiring at least 5 in each part. For differentiated evaluation, students are exempt from mandatory practice attendance, and their mastery of concepts will be assessed through an exam (65% of the final grade) and an individual substitute work (35% of the final grade), both requiring at least 5 points to pass.
